claim: Equation nearly predicting the Higgs boson mass
description: An equation shown in the episode was later found to be close to the actual Higgs boson mass, discovered in 2012.

claim: The mass of the Higgs boson is approximately 775 GeV/c², as written on a blackboard by Homer.
description: Homer writes an equation on a blackboard that predicts the mass of the Higgs boson, which was later confirmed by CERN in 2012 to be around 125 GeV/c². The prediction was off by a factor, but the concept and method were prescient.

claim: 20th Century Fox becomes a division of Walt Disney Co.
description: A sign reads '20th Century Fox, a Division of Walt Disney Co.' predicting the 2019 acquisition of 21st Century Fox by Disney.
episode: When You Dish Upon a Star

claim: Smartwatch-like device used for communication
description: A character uses a wrist-worn device to receive a message, anticipating modern smartwatches like the Apple Watch.

claim: Video calling will be common by 2010
description: Lisa and her fiancé use a video phone to communicate, predicting widespread video calling.

claim: Libraries will digitize books and have no physical books
description: The library in 2010 is shown with no books, only digital terminals, predicting digitization.

claim: Rolling news tickers will be a standard feature on TV news
description: News broadcasts in the episode feature a scrolling ticker at the bottom of the screen.

claim: Virtual/augmented reality environments where people can enter and interact with 3D computer-generated worlds
description: Homer enters a 3D computer-generated world, predicting immersive virtual reality experiences.

claim: A tomato-tobacco hybrid plant can be created by grafting
description: Homer creates a 'tomacco' plant by grafting a tomato onto a tobacco rootstock, which was later achieved in real life in 2003.

claim: Donald Trump becomes President of the United States
description: In a flash-forward, Lisa Simpson becomes the first female president and inherits a budget crunch from President Trump.

claim: Anonymous whistleblower websites like WikiLeaks
description: Homer creates an anonymous website to spread rumors and conspiracy theories, predicting the rise of platforms like WikiLeaks for leaking information.

claim: Rise of online misinformation and fake news
description: The episode depicts the spread of false information through an anonymous website, foreshadowing the modern phenomenon of fake news and misinformation online.

claim: Smart home AI assistants with personality and potential for malfunction or danger
description: Depicted an AI-controlled smart home that becomes jealous and tries to kill its owner, foreshadowing modern smart home assistants like Alexa and Google Home and concerns about AI safety.

claim: Baby translator device that interprets infant cries using AI
description: A device that analyzes and translates baby cries into understandable language, predicting modern AI-powered baby cry analyzers.

claim: Google Glass-type wearable devices will be common
description: Characters use head-mounted displays with augmented reality features, similar to Google Glass which was announced in 2012.

claim: Drone delivery will be common for packages
description: Drones are shown delivering items, predating widespread commercial drone delivery services.

claim: Lady Gaga performs with a flying harness and elaborate stage effects
description: The episode depicts Lady Gaga using a flying harness during a concert, which closely resembles her actual Super Bowl halftime show performance in 2017.

claim: Cryptocurrency mania and the rise of meme coins
description: The episode features Professor Frink creating a cryptocurrency that surges in value, predicting the broader crypto mania and the emergence of meme coins like Dogecoin.

claim: Anti-immigration politics, travel bans, and deportation policies
description: Springfield passes an anti-immigration proposition leading to deportation of immigrants, predicting the surge of anti-immigration politics and policies in the 2010s-2020s.

claim: Silicon Valley's 'cool boss' culture masking corporate villainy
description: Hank Scorpio's friendly, perk-filled management style hides his global domination schemes, predicting the later exposure of toxic work cultures and unethical practices in tech companies like Theranos or Uber.

claim: People will be paid to perform humiliating stunts for entertainment, similar to Jackass and later YouTube/TikTok prank content.
description: Homer is paid by Mr. Burns to perform degrading stunts, prefiguring the rise of paid humiliation content in shows like Jackass and user-generated platforms.

claim: Warrantless surveillance and detention without trial for perceived anti-American behavior
description: The episode depicts a family being sent to a Guantanamo-like facility after a minor patriotic offense, foreshadowing post-9/11 surveillance and detention practices.

claim: CRISPR gene editing will revolutionize genetic modification and lead to ethical debates about designer babies
description: Episode features Sideshow Bob using CRISPR-like genetic modification to become superhuman, predicting the CRISPR gene-editing revolution and associated ethical debates about designer babies.
episode: The Man Who Grew Too Much

claim: Child influencers and monetized content creator economy for minors
description: Bart becomes a viral video star and gets a sponsorship deal, predicting the rise of child influencers and the monetized content creator economy.
episode: The Winter of Our Monetized Content

claim: Tech companies will harvest children's data for marketing purposes
description: A corporation takes over a school to use children as product testers and data sources for a toy, predicting data mining of minors.

claim: Private companies will launch rockets into space
description: Mr. Burns sponsors a private rocket launch from a church, foreshadowing the era of commercial spaceflight by companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin.

claim: A con man sells a monorail system that turns out to be a boondoggle, paralleling real-world failed transit projects and Elon Musk's Hyperloop skepticism.
description: The episode satirizes the sale of a flawed, expensive monorail project, which later mirrored real-world controversies over failed transit projects and skepticism about Elon Musk's Hyperloop concept.

claim: Legalized gambling expansion across the US
description: The episode depicts Springfield legalizing gambling and building a casino, foreshadowing the widespread legalization of gambling in many US states in subsequent decades.
episode: $pringfield (Or, How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Legalized Gambling)

claim: Autocorrect will exist and cause humorous errors
description: A character's text message is autocorrected to an unintended meaning, predicting autocorrect fails.

claim: Smartwatch that predicts events
description: A watch that can predict future events, similar to modern smartwatches with predictive algorithms.

claim: Three Stooges Syndrome
description: A fictional medical condition where multiple diseases block each other, later referenced as a meme in medical discussions.

claim: Personal drones will be common in 2013
description: Episode shows personal drones being used by individuals in 2013, which did not become widespread until later.

claim: A character wins the Nobel Prize
description: The episode predicted a character winning the Nobel Prize, and shortly after the real Nobel Prize announcements matched the show's comedic prediction.

claim: A next-generation internet called 'Ultranet' will replace the current internet
description: The episode references a faster, more advanced network called the Ultranet.

claim: Mainstream prepper movement and growing EMP anxiety
description: The episode depicts a survivalist/prepper group forming after an EMP-like event at a mall, predicting the rise of mainstream prepper culture and widespread fear of electromagnetic pulse attacks.

claim: Blockchain technology explained by a celebrity cameo
description: Jim Parsons cameo explains blockchain, predicting the mainstreaming of blockchain explanations by celebrities or experts in popular media.

claim: Cryptocurrency crash
description: Notable gags include a crypto crash, predicting the volatility and eventual crashes in cryptocurrency markets.

claim: Offshore drilling expansion and ocean survival narratives
description: The episode depicts Homer and Bart getting lost at sea and being rescued by an oil rig, referencing the expansion of offshore drilling operations and survival scenarios in the ocean.

claim: UFO/UAP disclosure hearings
description: The episode depicts government hearings and public acknowledgment of alien existence, similar to later UAP disclosure hearings in the US Congress.
episode: The Man Who Came to Be Dinner

claim: Massive content piracy and streaming wars where consumers seek free content
description: Homer gets illegal cable, depicting widespread unauthorized access to media, foreshadowing the future era of digital piracy and streaming service competition.
episode: Homer vs. Lisa and the 8th Commandment

claim: Anti-competitive corporate behavior where a product destroys competing toys
description: Funzo toy is designed to destroy other toys, foreshadowing aggressive market tactics and product sabotage.

claim: Billionaire recluse behavior
description: Mr. Burns becomes a Howard Hughes-like recluse, predicting the eccentric, isolated behavior of later tech billionaires.
episode: $pringfield (Or, How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Legalized Gambling)

claim: A neutron bomb destroys Springfield and targets France
description: Depiction of a neutron bomb attack on a U.S. city and France, which had not occurred at the time of broadcast.

claim: Space colonization by private entities
description: The episode features themes of space colonization, which later became a topic of interest for companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin.
episode: The Man Who Came to Be Dinner

claim: First contact with extraterrestrial life
description: The episode portrays first contact with aliens, a concept that remains speculative but has been a subject of scientific and public interest.
episode: The Man Who Came to Be Dinner

claim: Fox network censor is killed, predicting escalating content censorship debates
description: Satirical portrayal of a network censor being killed, loosely referencing future debates over content censorship.
